f. Employment Opportunity
Nine business properties will be acquired as a result of the program. These businesses affected will be given relocation assistance and will be reestablished in most instances; however, the temporary loss of employment to some 44 individuals, during this process, is a negative factor that cannot be avoided. The exact extent of the temporary loss of employment cannot be assessed in terms of dollars or total numbers, but it is inevitable that it will occur in some cases. All nine indicate that they intend to relocate. None plan to go out of business as a result of the relocation.
On the other hand, job opportunity will increase from the amount of activities engendered by the plan. The employment activity relates not only to those individuals in the project area but also to individuals throughout the City and regional area. New construction of residential and business structures, street repair, and other phases of the public improvement activity, rehabilitation of private structure, administrative salaries and jobs related to these activities, represent the positive impact of the scheduled program during the execution stages. Some of the job opportunities will carry over into the periods following the initial execution stages and will become a permanent part of the community, e. g. maintenance of parks and open spaces, jobs in the redeveloped areas, and jobs relating to the continued upkeep of rehabilitated properties.
g. Schools
The redistribution of the population, resulting from new land use patterns, will have little impact on schools in the city system due to the present busing requirements. (See Part II, paragraph ). The short term negative impact of tax base reduction is the major factor in this category. This is more important to the school system than to the local City or County governments because the tax base is the principal source of revenue for the system, while the other forms of local government have other sources of revenue.
There are no known relationships between any private schools or private school system and the project itself, other than the favorable increase in the general economics of the area and neighborhood viability.
h. Police Protection
Police service will not be directly impacted by the planned project activities. Indirectly, it will be affected by the redistribution of population and the "thinning out" of the more densely populated areas along Penn Street. General
